_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE WIRES INTO THE STORE REFUSE AN UNMODELED KEY — run it
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. The store refusing a key it does not model closed the
loss at rest. Every wire into the store could still drop one first: an agent
calling `add_inventory_entry` with a `"modality"` got success and the key was
gone, and a manifest key the importer does not model vanished the same way.
Every map-shaped `Deserialize` type in every crate now refuses, a workspace
law holds it with a written exemption table, and every MCP tool schema says
TWO INJECTIONS, one per wire. Dropping the attribute from the MCP argument
type the adopter's case goes through must turn the workspace law red AND the
behavioural test that sends the key and reads the schema. Dropping it from the
facts manifest must turn the law red AND the manifest refusal test.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record

injections.name: an-agent-argument-reads-past-a-key
injections.why: the adopter's failure on the MCP wire: `add_inventory_entry` accepts a `modality` it does not model and the key never reaches the store, while the schema an agent reads invites it

injections.name: a-manifest-reads-past-a-key
injections.why: the other write path into the same facts: a manifest carrying a key the importer does not model imports without it, at exit 0. The MCP `import_facts` tool takes this type as its argument, so its schema stops saying `additionalProperties: false` too — measured on the first run of this sweep, where that red arrived undeclared
